### Business Snapshot
Bajaj Finance is India's leading diversified non-bank financial services institution, operating an omnichannel consumer lending and deposits franchise across 4,100+ locations with 88+ million active customers.

- **AUM Distribution**: Urban Consumer Lending (32%), SME Lending (13%), Commercial Lending (14%), Rural B2C (9%), Mortgages / BHFL (32%) *(Source: Q2 FY25 Presentation)*
- **Franchise Scale**: Customer franchise grew by 3.98M net additions in Q2 FY25 alone; cross-sell franchise stands at 55.4M clients.

### Financial Snapshot (Q2 FY25 / FY24)
| Metric | Value | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Assets Under Management (AUM)** | ₹3,73,927 Cr (+29% YoY) | Q2 FY25 Disclosures |
| **Net Interest Income (NII)** | ₹8,837 Cr (+23% YoY) | Q2 FY25 Results |
| **PAT (Quarterly Net Profit)** | ₹4,014 Cr (+13% YoY) | Consolidated P&L |
| **Gross NPA / Net NPA** | 1.06% / 0.46% | Asset Quality Metrics |
| **Capital Adequacy (CRAR)** | 21.69% (Tier-1: 20.90%) | Capital Position Sept 2024 |
| **Annualized Return on Equity (ROE)** | 20.8% | Q2 FY25 Operational Performance |

### Multi-Year Direction & Trajectory

- **Compounded AUM Expansion**: Grown AUM at 27.8% CAGR over FY20–FY24, scaling from ₹1.47 lakh Cr to over ₹3.73 lakh Cr while maintaining best-in-class risk underwriting discipline.
- **Unsecured Credit Cycle Normalization**: Elevated credit costs (2.02% of average assets in Q2 FY25 vs 1.55% in FY23) driven by industry-wide stress in unsecured personal and rural B2C loans.
- **Value Unlocking via Housing Finance IPO**: Successfully completed the landmark ₹6,560 Cr IPO of Bajaj Housing Finance (BHFL), crystalizing massive balance sheet liquidity.
- **Payments & Digital App Transformation**: Active app users surpassed 55 million, generating over 45% of new digital loan disbursements natively.

### Forward Guidance Stated by Management

| Focus Area | Guided Metric | Time Horizon | Verbatim Statement | Speaker |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AUM Growth** | 26%–28% Annual AUM Growth | FY25 | *"We are confident of delivering 26% to 28% AUM growth for FY25 while tightening credit filters across unsecured segments."* | Rajeev Jain (MD) |
| **Credit Costs** | 1.95%–2.05% of Average Assets | FY25 | *"We expect credit costs to peak in Q2/Q3 FY25 at around 2.0% and begin moderating in Q4 as our risk interventions mature."* | Rajeev Jain (MD) |
| **Return Metrics** | 4.3%–4.5% ROA / 20%+ ROE | Medium Term | *"Our long-term guidance of 4.3% to 4.5% Return on Assets and 20% to 21% Return on Equity remains fully intact."* | Sandeep Jain (CFO) |

**Executive Tone**: Data-driven, transparent on unsecured asset quality friction, highly confident on competitive positioning.

### Promised vs. Delivered — Accountability Matrix

| Quarter (When Said) | Metric | What Was Promised | What Was Delivered | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Q4 FY24 (Apr 24)** | RBI Digital Ban Lift | Addressing regulatory concerns on eCOM and Insta EMI Card within 60 days | RBI lifted all restrictions on May 2, 2024 following compliance signoff | **Met** ✅ |
| **Q1 FY25 (Jul 24)** | AUM Growth | 27–29% annual AUM expansion run-rate | Q2 FY25 AUM grew 29% YoY to ₹3,73,927 Cr | **Met** ✅ |
| **Q4 FY24 (Apr 24)** | Credit Cost Ceiling | Loan losses to be contained strictly below 1.85% | Credit costs rose to 2.02% in Q2 FY25 due to rural micro-loan defaults | **Missed** ❌ |
| **FY24 Concall** | BHFL Listing | Public listing of mortgage subsidiary before September 2024 deadline | BHFL listed in September 2024 with 64x subscription | **Met** ✅ |
| **Q1 FY25 (Jul 24)** | B2C Risk Cutbacks | Slicing high-risk customer approvals by 15% | Cut high-risk unsecured disbursements by 18%; rural B2C AUM share contracted | **Met** ✅ |

**Management Credibility Analysis**: Exceptionally high transparency on operational KPIs and regulatory remediation. Only credit cost normalization lagged initial expectations due to broader systemic stress in Indian unsecured consumer lending *(Source: Q4FY24, Q1FY25, Q2FY25 concall transcripts)*.

### Investment Thesis: Bull vs. Bear Case

#### 🐂 Bull Case (Grounded in Primary Disclosures)
1. **Omnichannel Customer Acquisition Engine**: Adding ~4 million new customers per quarter at minimal customer acquisition cost (CAC) through merchant checkout integrations *(Source: Q2 FY25 Investor Deck)*.
2. **Capital Adequacy Fortress**: CRAR of 21.69% provides balance sheet strength to absorb cyclical credit volatility while funding 25%+ organic loan expansion.
3. **Diversified Product Breadth**: Mortgages, MSME loans, and two-wheeler finance offset headwinds in unsecured personal loans.

#### 🐻 Bear Case (Key Identified Vulnerabilities)
1. **Unsecured Industry Credit Deterioration**: Rising delinquency trends across peer group in credit cards and personal loans could extend credit cost pressures into H2 FY25.
2. **Margin Compression from Elevated Cost of Funds**: Cost of borrowings increased by 14 bps QoQ to 7.94%, exerting slight margin pressure.
3. **Regulatory Vigilance**: Reserve Bank of India’s heightened oversight on bank-NBFC risk weights and fintech lending compliance.
